assembly_notes: The root is always the folded C-frame of the source screw clamp: a guided jaw on two rails, a threaded spindle on a registered vertical axis mate and a self-aligning pressure shoe. The frame adapts its head locally to the selected support family: arm families get a side clevis with bored bosses, the ratchet family additionally gets the toothed sector on the outer cheek, the gas-spring family a lower strut boss, the parallel linkage a second lower boss, and the column family a shelf plus a coaxial socket instead of the clevis. Every support candidate publishes one head seat (point plus accumulated world pitch) and every pad_head candidate consumes it through a vertical axis mate, so the wrist collar always stands upright regardless of the link pitch. All revolute joints are solved with mate_axes and registered with register_interface_mate. Pin joints use bored fork cheeks or sub-millimetre axial clearance instead of overlap allowances; no ctx.allow_overlap is used anywhere. The clamp actuation is its own slot: the screw candidate drives the shoe through a thread nut and spindle, while the over-centre cam candidate carries the shoe on a follower link driven by a cam lever that hangs below the guided jaw. The reach interface is also its own slot: the fixed mount pins the support base to the frame head, while the edge track interposes a carriage on frame-mounted rails and moves the whole head mount out in front of the jaw (host_x_off_m/host_z_off_m rebase every head-mount coordinate into the carriage frame).
